articles.title: Modeling 64-Hexagram Jingfang Najia & True Solar Time in TypeScript: Deterministic Calendar Engineering
articles.excerpt: Traditional East Asian calendar systems—such as the 60-term Sexagenary Cycle (Ganzhi), 24 Solar Terms, and 64-hexagram Jingfang Najia (Six-Line I Ching)—are often treated as fuzzy folklore, yet undern…
articles.body: Traditional East Asian calendar systems—such as the 60-term Sexagenary Cycle (Ganzhi), 24 Solar Terms, and 64-hexagram Jingfang Najia (Six-Line I Ching)—are often treated as fuzzy folklore, yet underneath they are pure deterministic state machines rooted in spherical astronomy and binary combinatorics. When building a zero-registration, edge-delivered charting workspace, we ran into four subtle engineering problems that cause web calculators to disagree on edge cases. Here is how we modeled them cleanly in TypeScript. 1. Solar Longitude vs. Civil Calendar Boundaries In the classical Four Pillars (BaZi) calendar, months do not switch on the 1st of a Gregorian or Lunar month.

It is sample text for testing display, not a translation of any real recording. Diagnose one thing at a time Garbled characters: reopen the file in a text editor and check its encoding.

articles.title: Building Sentinel: Uptime Monitoring with Signed Reports and Quorum
articles.excerpt: The problem with a single uptime checker Most uptime monitors are one process making one HTTP request from one location. That is enough to catch most outages, but it has two blind spots: the checker i…
articles.body: The problem with a single uptime checker Most uptime monitors are one process making one HTTP request from one location. That is enough to catch most outages, but it has two blind spots: the checker itself can go down, and regional network problems look like global outages. If my checker is in us-east and an ISP there has a routing issue, I could page my team at 3 AM for a problem that only a small share of users can see. I built Sentinel to explore whether a small network of independent validator nodes, each checking the same target from a different region and each signing its report, could reach a verdict by majority agreement and avoid false alarms from single-region noise. Here is what I learned.

articles.title: The MCP Inspector proxy trusted a redirect and inherited command execution
articles.excerpt: The MCP Inspector proxy trusted a redirect and inherited command execution Local developer tools sit in a useful but dangerous position. They run on a developer workstation, can often launch processes…
articles.body: The MCP Inspector proxy trusted a redirect and inherited command execution Local developer tools sit in a useful but dangerous position. They run on a developer workstation, can often launch processes, and connect to servers supplied by the same user. MCP Inspector was built to test those servers, so a hostile server was always part of its threat model. The advisory GHSA-g9hg-qhmf-q45m describes CVE-2025-58444 in @modelcontextprotocol/inspector before 0.16.6. A malicious redirect URI returned by an untrusted remote MCP server could inject script into the Inspector interface. The Inspector's proxy then provided a path from that script execution to arbitrary commands on the developer machine. The advisory rates it high at 8.6 under CVSS v4.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. Rather, it will go on display as a museum piece, according to company founder and CEO Elon Musk.
articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.
